79322.subject: 🔓 Claude was used to hack OpenAI
79322.body:

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8776fa6e-e2d0-4aec-9648-1bed6de3a659/GenAI_Daily_Banner.jpg?t=1778687445)
Caption: 


----------

----------
**Welcome back!** OpenAI built a version of GPT-6 for lawyers and the legal AI startups it competes with are already building on top of it. Anthropic revamped projects in the best update they had in a while. Three researchers used Claude Opus 5 to break into OpenAI's private code and got paid for it. Trump's state dinner for Xi Jinping has three AI bosses on the guest list.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **OpenAI:** What happens to legal AI startups now?

* **Anthropic:** What changed in your workflow?

* **Hacktron:** How much does breaking into OpenAI get you?

* **The White House:** Which three AI bosses made the guest list?


----------







----------
## OpenAI came for legal AI and its rivals signed up

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/99c47816-0a3c-4b00-9a51-f9b76734b54e/Sep_18_-_1.jpg?t=1789717587)
Caption: 

OpenAI released [Astra for Law](https://openai.com/index/astra-for-law/), a version of GPT-6 Astra tuned for legal work. It isn't a new model. It's the same one wrapped in a legal search index, legal writing instructions and controls for confidential client files.

The index covers US case law, statutes, regulations, court rules and administrative decisions across more than 230 million URLs.

**What OpenAI is claiming:**

* On 200 questions from Vals AI's Legal Research Bench, it passed the correctness check 54% of the time against 38.7% for Astra with plain web search.

* It found 24% more relevant cases and up to 54% more relevant passages from the right opinions.

Harvey and Legora, the legal AI startups OpenAI is supposedly competing with, are building on top of it as API customers.

Anthropic launched Claude for Legal in May and Google shipped Gemini for Legal in August. OpenAI hired Ironclad's founder in June to run this one.


----------







----------

Caption: 

Prepathon 2026 is two days of real conversations with folks from **Google, Amazon, OpenClaw, WooCommerce, Elementor** and 20+ more. 

AI, development, ecommerce, agencies, infrastructure, all of it. 

Day 1 has a dedicated session with OpenClaw's DevRel manager, which we're pretty excited about.

No fluff, no keynote theater. Just people

79321.subject: Nuance Labs Is Betting That Text Broke AI Conversation 🗣️
79321.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/nuance-labs-pitch-deck

👋 Hey, Linas here! Every day, I break down 3 stories shaping the future of FinTech & Artificial Intelligence - plus the money movements and trends worth tracking. First time here? 400k+ FinTech and AI leaders get this daily. Join them:
Nuance Labs just announced a $50 million Series A led by Lightspeed, with NVIDIA [ https://substack.com/redirect/037ddb90-ffcd-4245-ad5f-301a1b10037a?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] and Define Ventures joining Accel and South Park Commons.
The artificial intelligence company was founded last year by three former Apple researchers, has no product in market, and will not open a public research preview until later this year. The 13-slide deck behind the round contains no traction figures and no benchmarks. Oh, and its most important slide does not show a market size, a customer logo, or even a revenue chart. It shows a pipeline, then argues that text deletes the conversation.
That is the entire company in one idea.
Today’s visual agents listen to speech, turn it into text, ask a language model what to say, synthesize the answer as audio, and animate a face around the finished voice track. Each component can be excellent. The combined experience can still feel dead.
Nuance believes the problem is architectural. Text preserves the words but throws away the hesitation, gaze, rhythm, interruption, facial movement, and small acknowledgements that tell us whether another person is actually present. Its answer is a native audiovisual model that predicts what a person will say and how that person will move as one continuous stream.
If Nuance is right, “AI avatar” is too small a description. The company is essentially trying to build a human-interface model. That is a much bigger ambition, and a much harder one to prove than the deck admits.
Below, we go through the deck in detail and test its argument against everything that has happened since it was written. Here’s what is inside:
How the deck’s four acts are built, and why its restraint is both its best quality and its biggest weakness.
The NVIDIA benchmark, published after the deck, that measured how far cascaded avatars fall behind human timing, and what it means that the company behind the benchmark then invested.
The 6 competitors, from Tavus to ByteDance, that have moved toward Nuance’s thesis since the deck was written, including one that is attacking Nuance’s central claim from inside the architecture Nuance says cannot work.
Why the largest markets on slide 3 are the wrong first markets, which one passes the tests from our AI Monopoly Playbook [ https://substack.com/redirect/90bdadc4-6812-4e34-8b23-17c01f046cc0?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], and which two run directly into the EU AI Act.
